target_customer: Independent auto and collision repair shop owners
problem: Auto repair runs on calls, texts and emails with insurers, parts suppliers and customers, so shop staff lose time on busywork. Parrot agents call and coordinate with those people.
business_model: B2B software subscription, about $30K a year per shop for the first two signed shops
product_category: Vertical AI operating system for auto and collision repair

founders.name: Phillip Baek
education: Stanford biomedical research in high school
previous_startups: Startup automating multimodal workflows for biomedical researchers (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: Wrote lab automation software in high school.

founders.name: Liam McBride
education: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, computer engineering, left a master's program
previous_startups: Same biomedical workflow startup as cofounder
founders.background_notes: Applied machine learning and systems automation.

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice agents negotiating with insurers and integrations with CCC ONE, Audatex and Mitchell 1 are standard LLM engineering with hard parts around reliability and legacy system access.

defensibility.rationale: Becoming the system of record for a shop would be sticky, but the product is early and shop software vendors and phone agent vendors can add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Shop management vendors had already shipped AI receptionists (Shop-Ware, AutoLeap AIR) and others launched AI operating systems for shops, with dates not established. No incumbent action against Parrot found.

market_need_then: Auto repair has lagged in software adoption because work happens by phone and message. Two independent shops signed at about $30K a year according to the YC launch and a startup spotlight article, which shows early willingness to pay.

branding.domain_note: Uses useparrot.com, a prefix domain. Several other companies are called Parrot (a drone maker, a court reporting platform, a language app).

identity.logo: Not described in sources, orange accent on black, white and gray site
identity.visual_style: Black, white and gray base with bright orange accent and simple orange line icons
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, practical and benefit led, for example let Parrot handle the busy work

branding.brand_signature: Orange accent and the AI coworker framing

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly bird name that suits a calling agent, but it collides with several better known Parrot brands and only a startup spotlight article covers it.

pivots.from: Biomedical research workflow automation startup (earlier work of the founders)
pivots.to: AI operating system for auto and collision repair shops
pivots.why: The YC launch says the founders pivoted about three weeks before launch and worked alongside shop owners. The date is approximate.

outcome_analysis: Parrot is a two person Spring 2026 company that pivoted from biomedical workflow automation into collision repair and reports two shops signed at about $30K a year. Funding and exit are unknown, so the outcome is open. The wedge of calling insurers and suppliers is real, but shop software vendors and AI receptionist products crowd the space.
notes: Funding unverified: Dealroom shows $125K and VCBacked and FundedIQ report $500K pre-seed in June 2026, so no round is recorded. Website lists HQ as Austin, Texas while YC lists San Francisco. Competitor pages found (Shop-Ware AI receptionist, AutoLeap AIR, CarSignal) were undated or after the batch, so competition_at_founding is left empty. An unrelated Parrot raised an $11M Series A in 2023 (court reporting) and is not this company. Completeness pass: the 500K pre-seed (June 2026, FundedIQ and VCBacked) is now recorded and rests on aggregators only. Dealroom lists 125K as a seed instead; the figures conflict and are not summed.
